Your troops need your tactical talent to lead them to victory. Your mission? Be the first to reach the enemy headquarters or control more territories than your opponent. On your turn in Toy Battle, you either draw two toy troops or place a troop on the board and apply its effect. When a place a troop, you can place it on an empty base, a base that you control, a base that the enemy controls with a lower-valued troop than the one you're placing, or the enemy's headquarters; however, in all cases you must place on a location that has a continuous path to your own headquarters through bases that you occupy, that is, that have your troop on top. If you occupy bases that form a continuous path around a region, you claim the medals within this region. (You don't lose these medals if the enemy later occupies one of these bases.) The game ends as soon as you occupy your opponent's headquarters or win the required number of medals based on the current game board. If a player cannot draw or place a troop, the game ends, and whoever has the most medals wins. Number of players: 2 Game duration: 4 mn Complexity: 2 / 5 Play Toy Battle and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Overview The game plays over a series of turns, until the game end is triggered in one of three ways. If an HQ is captured by a Troop, the capturing player immediately wins. If through region control a player gains a certain number of medals as defined by the map, that player immediately wins. If a player cannot perform any more actions (e.g. they have no tiles to draw and cannot play any tiles), then the game ends. In this case, the player with the most medals wins. In the case of a tie, the player who triggered this end game condition loses. Each player has 24 troops--8 types with 3 of each. During set up, 4 troops are randomly removed from each player's reserve without the players knowing which tiles are removed. The removed tiles are likely different between the two players, creating a mysterious asymmetry. Troops Name Picture Strength Description Notes Kwak X Kwak has no effect, but may be placed on top of any enemy Troop. However, any enemy Troop may also cover it. Skully 1 You may draw 2 Troops from your reserve. If you already have 7 Troops on your rack, you draw only one. Capn 2 You may place 1 extra Troop following normal placement rules and apply its effect. Effects of Troops placed (including Capn) are triggered first, then any special base effects. Jumbo 3 You may choose 1 visible enemy Troop (adjacent to Jumbo) and discard it face up. Troops are adjacent if connected by a single section of path. Hook 4 You may ignore the connection rule and place Hook on any base whether or not it is connected to your H.Q. To place Hook on the enemy HQ (which is not a base), it must be connected to your HQ by your troops. XB-42 5 You may take, at random, 1 Troop from your opponent's rack and discard it face up. Star 6 You may draw 1 Troop from your reserve and place it on your rack. Roxy 7 No effect. Your Turn You can either: Draw 2 Troops from your reserve and place them on your rack. Your rack can hold up to 8 Troops maximum or Play 1 troop from your rack onto a space on the battlefield. You can place it anywhere that fulfills the following conditions: An empty base that is connected to your HQ (this means you must always follow a continuous path from your HQ (starting point) to the troop you are placing, passing only through bases you occupy) A base occupied by any of your troops A base occupied by an enemy troop with a lower strength than your troop Your opponent's HQ. (You cannot place a troop on your own HQ) Each troop has an effect that triggers after placement. If the troop was placed on a special base, you first fully complete the troop's effect before trigger the effect of the special base. The four tiles you randomly get rid of in the beginning of a game can literally lose/win you the game before you've even played one turn. Then you randomly draw 3 or 4 tiles to start. Then just to add more insult you have tiles in the game that cause the other player to randomly lose a tile?? Like wtf. [Rating: 1/10] Total and complete luck of the draw fest.  You are at the mercy of what you draw for playing any kind of strategy.

[Rating: 2/10] It's a nifty and clearly well-designed game that doesn’t excite me all that much. I'd be hard-pressed to tell you exactly why, so I'll deflect to my standard criticism of "there will be games where you have no choice but to succumb to the terrible luck of drawing tiles that you absolutely either do not need or cannot use". Lighting fast play time certainly helps quell those woes, though - not much of an investment which makes those cosmic shafts hurt less.

[Rating: 3/10] At a first glance Toy Battle looks like a cute light game: but the more you play it the more you realize how shallow it is. You’re in the hands of the tokens you’re drawing: and more likely than not, usually you don’t have the units you need available.  So the game turns into a luckfest: whoever is lucky enough to have the right units available at the right moment wins.  So much for a game.

[Rating: 3/10] This had a lot of hype but it's too light for me to enjoy. Super short and feels more like a kids game than something to bring to game night.
